source.title: HiPACE: Hierarchical Phase-Boundary Analysis and Controlled Evaluation of Feature Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Jin-Yuan Zhang; Peng-Ji He; Yin Yuan; He-Long Hu; Sheng-Shuo Jiao

page_placements.theme: Validity of absorption and splitting metrics and detectors

record.tranche_reason: The study tests hierarchical absorption and its structural consequences using a closed-form threshold, synthetic generators, and family-level decoder measurements rather than measuring whether a feature in a smaller SAE is partitioned among features in a larger SAE.
record.gate_note: The study reports a failed preregistered top-1 consensus proxy and family-direction intervention outcomes. These do not directly measure the size-dependent feature splitting named in the claim. Reported values for those related findings are recorded under fits_no_version. The study also discusses other absorption notions and prior studies; cited results are not recorded as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses its own methods rather than comparing dictionary sizes. Trained TopK SAEs on a synthetic hierarchical generator show that the sparsity budget decides between parent-direction and child coding (V6). Family-level parent–child decoder structure in a public Pythia-160m SAE aligns with WordNet families beyond sibling nulls (V3).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also call the preregistered proxy failure a 'metric-mediated non-transfer'. They say transfer fails under the consensus proxy and remains open under a K-corrected metric. They claim causal sufficiency only at the family-subspace level, not for a unique parent atom.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives an L0 cost threshold for a hierarchical Bernoulli generator and evaluates family-level decoder structure, controlled composition, and residual-stream interventions. It does not train successively larger SAEs on the same activations or trace feature-level input partitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Structural recovery depends on layer and direction statistic: L6 uses family mean and L11 uses centered PC1; the nonprimary L11 mean statistic falls inside the sibling null. The preregistered top-1 proxy also shows family-size baseline contamination.

fits_no_version.finding: Controlled composition of child prototypes raises parent-direction activation with active-child count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE parent-direction activation scales with the number of composed child activations in Pythia-160m.

fits_no_version.finding: Signed family-direction injections shift parent logits; parent and child directions have equal effects; sign-flip reverses the shift and random directions do nothing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Family-subspace directions recovered from SAE decoders causally shift parent-category logits.

fits_no_version.finding: The preregistered top-1 consensus firing proxy fails in the wrong direction across estimators, layers and the 410m replication. A 1/K baseline dominates it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instance-level top-1 consensus metrics of absorption are confounded by family size.

fits_no_version.finding: Matryoshka attenuates and Archetypal collapses the confounded proxy signal on Pythia.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE architecture changes per-sample firing-consensus absorption measures.

record.problems: The structural pipeline is tested on one model (Pythia-160m) and one public SAE family. The study itself notes that randomized siblings and partial correlations do not jointly match token frequency, decoder norm, hierarchy depth, and lexical similarity. Its structural results depend on layer-specific statistic selection, and its preregistered instance-level proxy is explicitly confounded by a 1/K baseline. The study also notes that the theoretical L0 objective and empirical TopK gating are not claimed to be equivalent.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted beyond the reported aggregates. The paper mentions a Pythia-410m external replication only for the preregistered proxy; it is included in r23. Individual plotted values for the synthetic stress sweep and variant results are not reported in the text, so only the stated aggregate summaries are recorded.

untested.parts: No comparison across dictionary sizes. No test that finer features partition a coarse feature's inputs or lie near its direction.
Uses one open SAE release (EleutherAI Pythia-160m 32k TopK) but tests no splitting. The 410m run covers only the failed firing proxy.
Nesting of families across dictionary sizes; whether the families arise from splitting; models other than Pythia-160m.

Not tested. The study's 'absorption' means a parent direction replaces child atoms, and it states this differs from Chanin et al.'s subset-skipping notion. No measure of parent latents failing to fire, and no size or sparsity fix.
No cross-size latent decomposition and no test for novel latents.

Whether splitting in real language-model SAEs is an objective artifact. Real-model Matryoshka/Archetypal comparisons use only the confounded firing proxy (r24, r25). The Matryoshka shift is confirmed only synthetically, without numbers in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The study's absorption notion (a parent direction replaces child atoms) is close to the inverse of feature splitting. It differs explicitly from V4's notion. V3 linkage is indirect: it shows hierarchy-specific decoder structure in one SAE, not families produced by splitting across sizes. r1 was unlinked because it is an exact theory check, not an SAE result.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of increasing SAE dictionary sizes; no test that larger-dictionary features partition the inputs of smaller-dictionary features or lie near their directions.

The structural analysis is on Pythia-160m SAEs. Pythia-410m is used only for an external replication of the preregistered proxy, not to test size-dependent splitting or the structural recovery pipeline across SAE families.

Measures family-level parent–child decoder structure against WordNet families, but does not test nested feature families across dictionary sizes or establish a hierarchy of successively finer concepts.
Does not test whether a parent latent fails to fire on inputs where a specific child takes over, or whether changing SAE size or sparsity fails to resolve that behavior.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents and no test for novel latents or canonical units across dictionary sizes.

Tests an objective-based absorption boundary on controlled hierarchical inputs and reports trained TopK and variant results, but does not establish that size-dependent feature splitting in language models is an SAE-objective artifact or compare splitting across objectives on the same activations.

rows.subject: hierarchical Bernoulli generator (HBG)
rows.operation_detail: Compared exact parent-absorption and child-coding costs across synthetic generator settings and recorded the 50% absorption onset.
rows.measure: Relative error of observed 50% absorption onset against λc(k⋆, α)
rows.value: Within ±15% on 30/30 cells; median absolute relative error 0.026; maximum 0.053; 900 runs
rows.note: This verifies the cost threshold in the controlled generator, not feature splitting across SAE dictionary sizes.
rows.check: This is an exact per-sample cost comparison under the study's own L0 derivation, not a trained SAE. It checks the study's theory against itself and shows nothing about what SAE training produces.

rows.subject: trained TopK SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Swept a controlled 4 × 4 generator sub-grid and compared trained-SAE crossover with the predicted boundary.
rows.value: Within one budget in 12 of 16 cells; four deviations at K = 16, where dictionaries retained a parent atom alongside child residuals
rows.locator: Section 4, Phase-Boundary Validation (RQ1); Appendix E, Figure 5
rows.note: The retained parent-plus-residual dictionaries are described as the mixed regime of Proposition 2.
rows.check: For V6 the relevant effect is that the objective's budget decides parent-vs-child allocation on hierarchical inputs. That holds in all 16 cells; the 4 K=16 deviations are still objective-driven mixed dictionaries. 'Partial' only describes agreement with the predicted boundary.

relation.reason: Its results bear directly on V3 and V6.

tranche.reason: It uses its own hierarchical generator and a decoder-gap statistic over WordNet families. There is no comparison of dictionary sizes. It bears on the same question.

source_check.notes: The structural correlations are partial Spearman (K controlled) of decoder gap vs the theory's predicted ordering. The tie to genuine WordNet families comes from the sibling nulls. Discovery sibling-null p is 0.005 (200 draws) and holdout p is 0.002 (500 draws); holdout CIs are not given. r8 and r9 repeat r6/r7. The L9/L3 remarks have no numbers. r21/r22 bundle mixed signs (+0.10; L11 -0.35).

statements.correction: Partial Spearman rho (K controlled) of the parent-child decoder gap against the theory's predicted ordering (threshold proxy) over WordNet families. Discovery (50 families): L6 mean gap -0.681 [-0.816,-0.448], L11 PC1 -0.933 [-0.955,-0.875], sibling-null p = 0.005 (200 draws). Holdout: L6 -0.605 (75 families), L11 -0.914 (41 families), sibling-null p = 0.002 (500 draws), no CIs given. The match to genuine WordNet families is shown by the randomized-sibling null.
statements.problem: All numbers are right, but the statement calls the correlation one between decoder gap and 'WordNet family structure'. The text says the gap 'recovers the predicted ordering', which is the phase-boundary threshold proxy across families, with family size K partialled out. 'Each had p = 0.002' holds only for the two holdout values.

statements.correction: Decoder gap vs predicted ordering (threshold proxy), partial Spearman controlling K: discovery L6 -0.681, L11 -0.933 (sibling-null p = 0.005, 200 draws); holdout L6 -0.605 (75 families), L11 -0.914 (41 families), sibling-null p = 0.002 (500 draws).
statements.problem: Like V3.support[1], it gives the correlation's partner as 'WordNet family structure'. In the text the partner is the theory's predicted ordering (threshold proxy), with K partialled out. 'p = 0.002 (r4-r9)' holds only for the holdout rows r6-r9. Discovery rows r4/r5 have p = 0.005.

statements.correction: No variant reaches rho <= -0.6. Estimators: +0.41, +0.10, +0.46. Layers L3/L6/L9/L11: +0.34, +0.41, +0.42, -0.35. MLP replication: Pythia-160m +0.12, Pythia-410m +0.49. The 1/K baseline dominates. Matryoshka attenuates and Archetypal collapses the proxy signal (Figure 5b).
statements.problem: 'Fails in the wrong direction across estimators, layers and the 410m replication' overstates. L11 gives -0.35, the predicted sign, which falls in the locked PARTIAL band (-0.6 < rho <= -0.3). The mean-of-singletons estimator gives +0.10, near zero. Every variant does miss the PASS threshold.
